newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: All Manila waterworks bids technically cleared.
newsitem.headline: All Manila waterworks bids technically cleared.

text.p: The Metropolitan Water and Sewerage System (MWSS) of the Philippines said on Wednesday that all bids for the privatisation of the utility were cleared by its technical committee.
MWSS administrator Angel Lazaro said the offers from four consortiums for two 25-year concessions to operate water services in Manila were found to be technically in order.
"Eight technical proposals were reviewed and eight were found to be responsive," Lazaro said.
The contracts will be awarded after the financial bids of the consortiums are opened on Thursday.
Four groups are vying for the two 25-year contracts to supply water to Metro Manila.

They are: the consortium of Bechtel Corp of the United States, United Utilities Plc and Ayala Corp; Lyonnaise des Eaux SA in collaboration with Benpres Holdings Corp ; Anglian Water Plc along with Australia Water Technologies Pty Ltd and Metro Pacific Corp; and Compagnie Generale des Eaux with Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc.
The privatisation will not yield any revenue for the government and the financial bids will be considered on the basis of the proposed water charges.
The bidder offering the highest discount to the present water rates would be the lowest bidder, MWSS officials said.

The upgrading of the system, which at present loses nearly 50 percent of supply due to leaks and pilferage, is expected to involve an investment of about $7 billion, which has to be borne by the winning bidder.
The winner will also assume the debts of MWSS, officials said.
The technical bids approved on Wednesday referred to the kind of infrastructure the bidders proposed to set up to meet the goal of providing an efficient water supply system to the metropolis.
The two concessions, for east and west Manila, are expected to serve a population of 11 million.
At present MWSS is able to supply water to just 65 percent of the population with an average availability of 16 hours per day.

Under terms of the privatisation contract, the winner is expected to cover 85 percent of the population within five years with availability rising to 24 hours. In 10 years, the coverage is expected to rise to 98 percent.
MWSS' sewerage operations now cover just nine percent of the population and the concessionaires are expected to take it up to 83 percent in 25 years.
The MWSS privatisation process has been dogged by controversy with Manila Regional Trial Court still considering a petition to halt the deal.
The case filed by former and current officials of Rizal province as well as a former military general is expected to be heard later on Wednesday.
The group says President Fidel Ramos' authority to privatise MWSS, given by the Water Crisis Act, lapsed as of December 1995.
